segments.text: YES, MA'AM. MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC ARE ALLOWED A REASONABLE OPPORTUNITY AT THE BEGINNING OF THE CRA MEETING TO ADDRESS ANY ITEM ON THE AGENDA BEFORE THE CRA TAKES OFFICIAL ACTION ON AN ITEM. HOWEVER, A THREE-MINUTE TIME LIMIT APPLIES TO ALL SPEAKERS PROVIDING PUBLIC COMMENT, UNLESS SUCH TIME FRAME IS MODIFIED BY A VOTE OF THE CRA BOARD. SPEAKERS AND MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC ARE ALSO REMINDED THAT THEY ARE TO REFRAIN FROM DISRUPTIVE BEHAVIOR, INCLUDING MAKING VULGAR OR THREATENING REMARKS OR MAKING OR CAUSING DISRUPTIVE NOISES OR SOUNDS OR DISPLAYING SIGNS OR GRAPHICS. SPEAKERS ARE ALSO REMINDED TO REFRAIN FROM LAUNCHING PERSONAL ATTACKS. PERSONS FAILING TO COMPLY WITH THE CRA'S RULES MAY ALSO BE RULED OUT OF ORDER AND, AT THE DISCRETION OF THE CHAIR, MAY BE REMOVED FROM THE CHAMBERS FOR THE REMAINDER OF THAT DAY'S MEETING. FINALLY, CRA BOARD MEMBERS ARE REMINDED THAT THEY SHOULD REFRAIN FROM ENGAGING A SPEAKER UNDER PUBLIC COMMENT. THE CITY COUNCIL RULES AS REVISED JUNE 6, 2024, ARE NOW IN EFFECT FOR THE CRA BOARD UNLESS OTHERWISE EXEMPTED BY OR OVERRIDDEN BY THE CRA BYLAWS.

segments.text: THANK YOU VERY MUCH. NEXT SPEAKER, PLEASE START WITH YOUR NAME. YOU HAVE THREE MINUTES. MITA MARTINEZ, AKA, MIMI. I AM A CURRENT EAST TAMPA CRA COMMUNITY ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEMBER. segments.text: THANK YOU. NEXT SPEAKER, PLEASE START WITH YOUR NAME. YOU HAVE THREE MINUTES. MY NAME IS VICKY TONG. NOT JUST ACROSS THE COUNTRY BUT I.C.E. HAS ALREADY BEEN AND HARMED THE TAMPA BAY AREA. I.C.E. IS TARGETING LATINO SMALL BUSINESSES AND COMMUNITIES IN TAMPA. I.C.E. MURDERS BOTH ADVOCATES OF IMMIGRANT RIGHTS LIKE RENEE GOOD AND ALEX PRETTI, AS WELL AS IMMIGRANTS LIKE LORENZO SALGADO ARAUJO AND JOAN SEBASTIAN GUERRERO. IN 2025, THE SUPREME COURT RULED THAT I.C.E. FOR ALL THESE REASONS AND MORE, I'M HERE TO DEMAND THAT TAMPA CITY COUNCIL COUNCILORS ACT IN THE INTEREST OF THEIR CONSTITUENTS, MANY OF WHOM ARE IMMIGRANTS THEMSELVES AND TAKE A STAND AGAINST TRUMP AND DESANTIS BY PASSING AN ORDINANCE TO END TAMPA'S 287(g) AGREEMENT. THANK YOU.

AND TPD TO COLLABORATE ENDANGERS ALL OF US WHOM YOU HAVE SWORN TO PROTECT. ALSO PARTAKING IN 287(g) AGREEMENT USING I.C.E. ENFORCEMENT TACTICS, CONTRADICTS TAMPA'S HUMAN RIGHTS ORDINANCE. segments.speaker: NAYA YOUNG
segments.text: THANK YOU. NEXT SPEAKER, PLEASE START WITH YOUR NAME. YOU HAVE THREE MINUTES. MY NAME IS COURTNEY PREKOPIS. I COME BEFORE YOU TODAY ON BEHALF OF THE LEAGUE OF WOMEN VOTERS OF FLORIDA. THE LEAGUE URGES THE CRA AND THE GREATER CITY OF TAMPA TO END THEIR 287(g) AGREEMENT. THESE 287(g) AGREEMENTS ARE NOT MANDATED FOR CITIES, DESPITE THE STATE'S DECEPTIVE CLAIMS TO THE CONTRARY. OUR REQUEST IS FOR THE CITY OF TAMPA TO END THEIR VOLUNTARY 287(g) AGREEMENT. THAT REQUEST IS NOT PARTISAN. IT REFLECTS THE LEAGUE OF WOMEN VOTERS ENDURING COMMITMENT TO CIVIL LIBERTIES, EQUAL JUSTICE, FAMILY UNITY, AND RESPONSIVE GOVERNMENT, YOURSELVES INCLUDED, THAT SERVES THE ENTIRE COMMUNITY. THANK YOU.

THE ATLANTA CONSTITUTION WAS A WHITE NEWSPAPER, AND THEY EXPLAINED HOW THEY SHOULD PROBABLY FIND SOME BLOCK REPORTERS OUT THERE TO GO SHARE THE INFORMATION. I'M GOING TO SHARE ONE MORE THING. I HAVE AN EVENT NEXT WEEK, BEAT OF TAMPA BAY ON WEDNESDAY. AND THEN MY FIRST SPONSORED EVENT, UNLOCK YOUR LEGACY ON SATURDAY, NEXT SATURDAY. THANK YOU. IT'S FOR TEENS ONLY. THANK YOU.

segments.text: THANK YOU. NEXT SPEAKER. START WITH YOUR NAME. YOU HAVE THREE MINUTES. MY NAME IS ALISON HEWITT. I'M A THIRD GENERATION RESIDENT AND A BUSINESS OWNER IN EAST TAMPA. segments.text: THANK YOU. NEXT SPEAKER, PLEASE START WITH YOUR NAME. YOU HAVE THREE MINUTES. CONNIE BURTON. segments.text: THANK YOU SO MUCH. WE'LL BE GETTING A LOT OF PUBLICITY ABOUT ALL OF THAT. THE THIRD THING I HAVE IS THE NEWSLETTER. IT'S ON YOUR DESK UP THERE ON THE DAIS. segments.text: DO WE MAIL THESE TO ANYBODY AS WELL?

segments.speaker: BRENDA THROWER
segments.text: WE DON'T MAIL THEM. BECAUSE IT'S VERY EXPENSIVE. WE COULD, BUT WE HAVEN'T DONE THAT IN THE PAST. segments.speaker: MELISA MARTINEZ
segments.text: ONE LAST TIME. [ APPLAUSE ] GOOD MORNING.

segments.speaker: ALAN CLENDENIN
segments.text: WE'RE NOT APPLAUDING THAT YOU'RE LEAVING.

segments.speaker: MELISA MARTINEZ
segments.text: MELISA MARTINEZ FOR ONE LAST TIME. SENIOR PROJECT SUPERVISOR FOR THE TAMPA CRA. THANK YOU SO MUCH. I REALLY APPRECIATE THE TIME. I'VE BEEN WORKING FOR THE CITY FOR 18 YEARS. segments.speaker: BRENDA THROWER
segments.text: SHE'S STILL WORKING, SO SHE WILL BE HERE FOR THE MEETING. WE HAVE A FEW ITEMS THAT WE MAY NEED MS. MARTINEZ TO BE A PART OF. THAT CONCLUDES THE DIRECTOR'S REPORT. ARE THERE ANY QUESTIONS?

segments.speaker: NAYA YOUNG
segments.text: BOARD MEMBER MANISCALCO.

segments.speaker: GUIDO MANISCALCO
segments.text: I'VE ALWAYS SUPPORTED THE JACKSON HOUSE. I'M GLAD TO SEE DR. COLLINS HERE, WHO HAS BEEN A CHAMPION SINCE BEFORE DAY ONE. RECENTLY, WE CELEBRATED THE BEGINNING OF THE RESTORATION OF THE GUIDA HOUSE IN WEST TAMPA OUTSIDE THE CRA BOUNDARIES. SOME FOLKS WERE ASKING, WHAT ABOUT THE JACKSON HOUSE? WELL, WE DON'T OWN IT. THE GUIDA HOUSE IS A PROPERTY THAT THE CITY OF TAMPA DOES HAVE. THE JACKSON HOUSE IS PART OF THE FOUNDATION THAT'S MORE COMPLICATED LAYERS. BUT AGAIN, I'M EXCITED THAT THIS IS MOVING FORWARD THAT WE CONTINUE TO MOVE FORWARD. WE'VE ALWAYS SUPPORTED IT UP HERE. ONCE IT'S DONE, IT'S GOING TO BE VERY, VERY EXCITING. THAT'S IT. MOVE THE RESOLUTION.

segments.speaker: CHARLIE MIRANDA
segments.text: SECOND.

segments.speaker: NAYA YOUNG
segments.text: BOARD MEMBER CARLSON.

segments.speaker: BILL CARLSON
segments.text: I'VE BEEN A HUGE ADVOCATE FOR THE JACKSON HOUSE FOR A LONG TIME. TALKED TO LINDA SAUL-SENA, WHEN THE LAST MAYOR TRIED TO TEAR DOWN, LINDA CAME IN TO CITY COUNCIL AND CITY COUNCIL SAVED THE JACKSON HOUSE. BUT NOTHING HAS HAPPENED SINCE THEN. THERE'S BEEN VERY LITTLE HAPPENING TO IT. IT'S FALLING APART. THERE ARE SOME DOCUMENTS HERE THAT SAY WE ALLOCATED THIS MONEY IN 2022. AS BEST I CAN TELL, IT WAS 2019. YOU CAN BLAME THE ADMINISTRATION OR WHOMEVER FOR NOT ADVANCING THE MONEY. THE JACKSON HOUSE FOUNDATION THOUGHT IT WAS COMING FROM THE CITY BECAUSE THE MAYOR'S PRESS CONFERENCE. BUT MY CONCERN IS NOTHING IS HAPPENING. EVERY TIME THE JACKSON HOUSE FOUNDATION SAYS THAT THERE IS A REASON WHY THEY CAN'T DO ANYTHING, WE CORRECT THAT PROBLEM AND THEN THEY COME UP WITH A NEW EXCUSE, CORRECT THAT PROBLEM, NEW EXCUSE AND WE CORRECT THAT PROBLEM. I DON'T HAVE CONFIDENCE IN THEM FIXING THIS BUILDING. WE SUGGESTED BUYING IT FROM THEM IN THE PAST. WE SUGGESTED TAKING IT OVER. BUT THEY GET LOTS OF PUBLICITY AND BLAME EVERYBODY ELSE FOR NOT FIXING THE BUILDING BUT THE BUILDING IS GOING TO FALL APART. I THINK WE OUGHT TO ADD A CLAUSE OR SENTENCE, TALKED TO CLIFF ABOUT THIS EARLIER, THAT SAYS IF THEY DON'T REPAIR THE BUILDING WITHIN A YEAR THAT WE WITHDRAW THIS MONEY. IT'S BEEN SITTING THERE SINCE 2019 IN AN ACCOUNT. AND THE JACKSON HOUSE FOUNDATION HAS GOT TO DO SOMETHING OR THEY NEED TO SELL IT TO SOMEBODY OR TURN IT OVER TO SOMEBODY WHO IS GOING TO SAVE IT. IF THEY DON'T INTEND TO SAVE IT, WHICH APPEARS TO BE TRUE, THEN THEY NEED TO LET SOMEBODY ELSE SAVE IT. IF THE CITY CONTROLLED THIS BUILDING, WE WOULD HAVE SAVED IT BY NOW. I'M TIRED OF SEEING THE POSTS OVER AND OVER AGAIN ABOUT HOW THE CITY IS NOT SAVING IT WHEN WE ALLOCATED THE MONEY THROUGH THE CRA MANY, MANY YEARS AGO. I WOULD MAKE A MOTION TO ADD A CLAUSE -- CLIFF SAID WE CAN ADD THIS VERBALLY -- ADD A CLAUSE THAT SAYS THIS CONTRACT AND MONEY -- KEEP IN MIND, IT'S BEEN AVAILABLE SINCE 2019 -- THAT IT EXPIRES A YEAR FROM NOW IF THE JACKSON HOUSE FOUNDATION HAS NOT SUBSTANTIALLY RENOVATED THE BUILDING.

segments.speaker: NAYA YOUNG
segments.text: MIRANDA AND THEN YOU.

segments.speaker: CHARLIE MIRANDA
segments.text: THANK YOU, MADAM CHAIR. I'M SPEAKING FOR NOT ONLY MYSELF BUT OTHER COUNCIL MEMBERS NOT HERE THAT I'VE SERVED WITH IN THE PAST. NOT ONE EVER HAS VOTED AGAINST IT THAT I KNOW OF. SOME THINGS IN LIFE TAKE A LITTLE LONGER. SOMETIMES WHEN IT TAKES A LITTLE LONGER, YOU DO A LITTLE BETTER. THANK YOU VERY MUCH.

segments.speaker: NAYA YOUNG
segments.text: BOARD MEMBER CLENDENIN.

segments.speaker: ALAN CLENDENIN
segments.text: I THINK I SHARE EVERYBODY'S FRUSTRATION WITH THE SPEED OF THIS PARTICULAR ISSUE. WE SAW SOME OF THE RECENT DAMAGE JUST IN THE LAST COUPLE OF WEEKS WITH A CAVE-IN ON THE SIDE OF THE HOUSE. IT IS EXTRAORDINARILY FRUSTRATING THAT IT'S TAKING SO LONG. I UNDERSTAND SOME OF THE CHALLENGES IN THE PAST WITH THE RIGHT-OF-WAYS AND ALL THAT. I AGREE WITH BOARD MEMBER CARLSON TODAY THAT WE PROBABLY HAVE TO HAVE SOME KIND OF STOP INSTEAD OF ONGOING THING. THERE NEEDS TO BE SOME TYPE OF DEADLINE ON THIS TO MOVE FORWARD. IF THIS GOES ON ANY FURTHER, THERE WON'T BE A JACKSON HOUSE TO RESTORE.

segments.speaker: NAYA YOUNG
segments.text: BOARD MEMBER VIERA, AND THEN I WANT TO ALLOW -- WE DO HAVE THE JACKSON HOUSE FOUNDATION HERE.

segments.speaker: LUIS VIERA
segments.text: THANK YOU, MADAM. THE SENTIMENTS EXPRESSED BY COUNCILMAN CARLSON I'M PUTTING AN ADDITIONAL SENSE OF URGENCY, OBVIOUSLY VERY WELL TAKEN. I WOULD LIKE TO GO FORWARD VOTING THE REPRESENTATIVES OF THE JACKSON HOUSE. THE SENTIMENTS ARE WELL TAKEN. BUT I WOULD LIKE TO HEAR REBUTTAL, WHATEVER YOU WANT TO CALL IT.

segments.speaker: NAYA YOUNG
segments.text: DR. COLLINS. FOUNDATION INC. JACKSON HOUSE FOUNDATION. SUPPORT. IT'S AMAZING THAT I FOUND OUT FROM COUNCILMAN MAYBE TWO YEARS AGO, THREE YEARS THAT WE EVEN HAD THE MONEY. WE DIDN'T KNOW WE HAD THE MONEY. EVER SINCE WE FOUND OUT WE'VE HAD THE MONEY, WE'VE BEEN GRATEFUL. WE'VE ACKNOWLEDGED IT AND WE'VE DONE EVERYTHING THAT WE'VE BEEN TOLD TO DO TO GET IT. I NEED TO SAY THIS AND I NEED TO SAY IT NOW. AND IT'S NOT NEGATIVE. I HOPE IT'S POSITIVE. WHILE THE INTENT MAY HAVE ALWAYS SEEMED AS THOUGH THERE WAS AN INTEREST IN THE JACKSON HOUSE, THERE WAS ALWAYS SOMETHING WORKING BEHIND THE SCENES. WE WERE NOT BLAMING THE CITY. WE WERE NOT BLAMING ANYONE. WE WERE GIVING THE FACTS. AND WE NEED PEOPLE TO UNDERSTAND THAT'S WHAT WE WERE DOING. WE HAVE HIRED AN ARCHITECT. WE HAVE DONE THE DESIGN PLANS. THE HOUSE COLLAPSED ABOUT THIS TIME LAST YEAR. WE DID EMERGENCY REPAIR WORK ON IT. EVERYONE WHO SAY THEY GAVE US MONEY, WE STILL DO NOT HAVE THE MONEY AND WE'RE TRYING TO MAKE SURE THAT WE CAN GET THAT PAID FOR. I NEED TO SAY THIS, IN ADDITION TO THAT, WE ARE RAISING MONEY SO THAT WE WILL HAVE THE FINANCES. WE HAVE ALSO GONE THROUGH A PLETHORA OF CONTRACTORS IN ORDER TO GET SOMEONE WHO IS WILLING TO DO THE WORK ON THE JACKSON HOUSE. WE ARE FORTUNATE THAT WE HAVE THE COMPANY. WE HAVE SENT THE CONTRACT TO THE CITY, TO THE COUNTY, TO THE STATE WHO IS ALSO LOOKING AT IT FROM A FEDERAL PERSPECTIVE. THIS IS NOT JUST A, WE ARE SO HAPPY WITH WHAT'S HAPPENING AT THE GUIDA HOUSE IN THE AREA OF THE PARK. WE ARE NOT HOLDING UP NOR BLAMING ANYONE. WE ARE TRYING TO JUMP THROUGH EVERY HOOP THAT WE'VE BEEN GIVEN. AND LOOK BACK EVERY TIME WE ACHIEVE ONE, WE GET ANOTHER ONE. BUT WE'RE NOT STOPPING. WE'RE GOING TO REBUILD THE JACKSON HOUSE AT 851 ZACK STREET. IF THE INTENT IS TO MAKE SURE, COUNCILMAN, ALL OF YOU, THAT WE ARE DOING WHAT WE SAID WE'RE GOING TO DO, WE'RE GOING TO ASK YOU TODAY TO DO ONE THING FOR US. EXPEDITE US GETTING THE FUNDS SO THAT WE CAN MOVE FORWARD. WE HAVE FUNDS FROM A NUMBER OF ENTITIES. WE HAVE PEOPLE OUTSIDE OF THE STATE OF FLORIDA WHO HAVE BEEN ABLE TO SEE SOME OF THE PRESS RELEASES THAT WE'VE BEEN DOING OVER THE YEARS, AND THEY HAVE THEIR OWN FOUNDATION AND THEY HAVE SENT US MONEY TO HELP US WITH DAY-TO-DAY OPERATION AND SUMS OF MONEY SUFFICIENT THAT WE CAN ACTUALLY WORK WITH, BUT NOT SUFFICIENT ENOUGH TO BUILD A HOUSE. THE CONTRACT JUST GOT BACK FROM THE STATE OF FLORIDA. WE HAVE IT. WE MET WITH THE CONTRACTOR WITH THE, I CALL IT THE BREACH IN THE HOUSE GOING ON NOW. WE ARE WORKING WITH CITY STAFF AND THE STATE WITH A MEETING TODAY TO MAKE SURE WE CAN MOVE FORWARD. THERE'S ONE THING I WANT EVERYBODY TO UNDERSTAND. WE COULD HAVE BUILT THIS HOUSE A LONG TIME AGO. COULD HAVE BUILT IT MUCH CHEAPER AND IT WOULDN'T HAVE BEEN THE HISTORIC JACKSON HOUSE. IT WOULD HAVE BEEN THE JACKSON HOUSE 851 ZACK STREET. OUR HANDS ARE TIED. EVERY MONTH I GET A COMMUNICATION FROM FEMA. WE HAVE TO REPORT TO THEM. THEY WANT THE BUDGET. THEY WANT TO KNOW WHAT WE'RE DOING. WE'RE JUMPING THROUGH ALL OF THE HOOPS. WE'RE DOING EVERYTHING WE'VE BEEN TOLD TO DO. WHAT WE WOULD ASK TODAY AND THANK YOU IN ADVANCE FOR PASSING THIS SO THAT THE CONTRACTOR THAT WE HAVE AND WILL PROBABLY BE SIGNING, WISH WE COULD HAVE SIGNED IT THE 1st OF JULY, BUT HOPEFULLY WE'LL BE SIGNING IT AND STATE STAFF WHO HAVE BEEN ABSOLUTELY EXCELLENT. SECRETARY OF INTERIOR AND ALL AT THE STATE OF FLORIDA WHO WORKING WITH US. THEY SAID THEY KNOW TAMPA WILL WORK WITH YOU AND DO THIS. WE'VE HAD THEIR GRANT LONGER THAN WE'VE HAD THE CRA GRANT AND KNOW THAT WE HAD IT. SO WHATEVER YOU WANT TO PUT IN NOW, PROBABLY CAN SAY OKAY A YEAR. WE ASK THAT YOU NOT PUT THAT ON US. JUST GET US MONEY. WE EVEN CAME TO YOU BEFORE AND SAID TO YOU THIS IS A MILLION DOLLARS. WE'RE TALKING ABOUT WHAT IS PROBABLY A FULL MILLION DOLLAR PROCESS. AND SINCE IT WAS ALMOST FIVE YEARS AGO, WE ASKED YOU TO ALLOW US TO CHANGE IT AND INCREASE IT. YOU SAID, WELL, GO AHEAD, AS SOON AS YOU SIGN THE CONTRACT, AS SOON AS THE CONTRACTOR GIVE YOU A BUDGET, BRING IT BACK. WE ARE HERE. WE WILL ALWAYS BE HERE. THE PREVIOUS COMPLAINT WAS WE NEVER CAME. THAT'S WHY WE START TRYING TO COME REGULAR. WE WANT TO DO WHATEVER IT IS WE NEED TO DO. I THANK EACH AND EVERY ONE OF YOU FOR THE SUPPORT AND VOTES YOU HAVE GIVEN US. I THANK THE MAYOR AND HER ADMINISTRATION, ALL OF THE LEGAL STAFF, EVERYBODY WHO HAS WORKED DILIGENTLY WITH US. I HAVE TO TELL YOU, I EVEN THANK THE ACCARDIS, AFTER THREE TO FOUR YEARS, FINALLY GAVE US THE EASEMENT ON THE EAST AND WEST SIDE SO WE WOULD BE ABLE TO MEET WITH YOU GUYS, TOLD US CODE, FOUND OUT SUBSEQUENTLY, WE COULD HAVE BUILT IT WITHOUT THE EASEMENT. HEAR CITY OFFICIALS MAKE COMMENTS ABOUT HOW THE HOUSE SHOULD BE SOLD AND DIDN'T HAVE A MEETING WITH US TO TALK TO US ABOUT WHERE WE ARE IN THE PROGRESS, THAT FOR ME AND I'M NOT SPEAKING ON BEHALF OF DR. COLLINS. I AM SPEAKING ON BEHALF OF DR. ANGELA SCOTT, WHO IS THE CHAIR OF THE RESTORATION PROJECT THAT HAS BEEN WORKING DILIGENTLY WITH THE CITY, THE COUNTY, AND THE STATE. SO FOR SOMEONE TO MAKE A STATEMENT THAT WE'RE NOT DOING WHAT WE'RE SUPPOSED TO DO AND DIDN'T HAVE A CONVERSATION WITH US, I THINK THAT'S UNFAIR TO MAKE THOSE PUBLIC COMMENTS. SO GOING ON RECORD, WE ARE DOING WHAT WE ARE SUPPOSED TO BE DOING. TALK TO YOUR STAFF, TALK TO PEOPLE IN THE CITY TO KNOW WHAT WE'RE DOING TO ACHIEVE THIS GOAL. I DO KNOW PEOPLE IN THE COMMUNITY ARE SAYING THINGS ON SOCIAL MEDIA. THAT IS THE NEW FORMAT OF COMMUNICATION, AND THAT IS OKAY. I DON'T HAVE TO PANIC WHEN THE CITY PANIC. I DON'T HAVE TO PANIC WHEN THE PEOPLE PANIC BECAUSE I KNOW WE'RE DOING WHAT WE'RE SUPPOSED TO DO. THIS HOUSE WILL BE REBUILT IN THE GOVERNANCE WE HAVE, AUTHORITY TO DO IT WITH. WE WILL KEEP THE HISTORICAL STATUS AND WE ARE WORKING WITH THE DIFFERENT FUNDING SOURCES THAT WE HAVE. SO PLEASE SPEAK TO US. I KNOW ONE COUNCILPERSON UP HERE WHO TALKS TO ME REGULARLY TO FIND OUT WHAT'S GOING ON. AND THANK YOU, NAYA YOUNG. AND THANK YOU, MR. CARLSON, BECAUSE WE DID ASK YOU FOR A MEETING. WE CALLED YOU. YOU WAS WILLING TO MEET WITH US. AND WE MET WITH YOU AND YOU EVEN SAID ON THE MEDIA THAT ANYTHING HAPPEN, WE WILL GIVE THEM THE ADDITIONAL MONEY AND MAKE IT HAPPEN. AND WHILE YOU'VE NOT BEEN ABLE TO COME THROUGH FOR WHATEVER REASON, WE'RE ASKING YOU TO COME THROUGH NOW. SO WE THANK YOU. WE THANK ALL OF YOU BECAUSE WE'VE HAD A TOTAL VOTE, SEVEN RIGHT, WE'VE HAD A 7-0 VOTE THAT YOU GUYS SUPPORTED US. AND WE THANK YOU FOR THAT. WE NEED TO LET YOU KNOW WE HAVE NOT TAKEN IT FOR ADVANTAGE. WE'VE ACTUALLY WORKED, AND WE'VE DONE EVERYTHING. THE HOUSE WILL BE BUILT. 851 EAST ZACK STREET. AND WE'RE KEEPING IT AS A HISTORIC HOUSE. AND THE RESTRICTIONS ON US FOR HISTORIC HOUSE IS ASTRONOMICAL. WE DON'T MIND SHOWING IT TO YOU. WE SOMETIMES PULL OUR HAIR OUT. THEY CALL ME AND I HAD TEN MINUTES TO GET TO THE HOUSE, WHEN WAS IT, YESTERDAY. I WAS LATE. IT TOOK ME 15, BUT I GOT THERE WITH THE INTENT OF NOT EVEN HAVING A GLASS OF WATER, TAKING MY BLOOD PRESSURE PILL. I TOOK WHAT I NEEDED TO DO. I DIDN'T GET BACK HOME UNTIL 2:00. WE ARE WORKING. WE ARE GOING TO CONTINUE TO WORK DILIGENTLY. WE APPRECIATE WHAT CRA HAS DONE. WE APPRECIATE WHAT THE BOARD OF THE CITY COUNCIL HAVE DONE SINCE YOU GUYS ARE REALLY TWO DIFFERENT ENTITIES. WE THANK YOU AND WE ASK YOU TO CALL US ANYTIME. WE ARE AVAILABLE FOR YOU 24/7. BECAUSE THAT'S WHAT IT'S GOING TO TAKE FOR THE JACKSON HOUSE TO BE REPLACED. WE ARE NOT BLAMING ANYONE. WE ARE WORKING ON EVERYTHING.

segments.speaker: NAYA YOUNG
segments.text: THANK YOU, LADIES. BOARD MEMBER VIERA, YOU WANTED TO SPEAK. DO YOU STILL HAVE COMMENTS? THEN WE'LL GO TO CARLSON AND ALAN.

segments.speaker: LUIS VIERA
segments.text: MY VIEW IS THAT SOMETHING THAT PUTS CONTRACTUALLY BOUND CUT OFF, ESPECIALLY AFTER HEARING FROM THESE TWO BOARD MEMBERS AND WOMEN, I WOULD PREFER SOMETHING THAT IS MORE ASPIRATIONAL, WHAT HAVE YOU, AS OPPOSED TO SOMETHING CONTRACTUALLY BOUND. I THINK IT'S SOMETHING, AGAIN, AFTER HEARING THEM OUT. THAT'S SOMETHING I'M WILLING TO SUPPORT.

segments.speaker: NAYA YOUNG
segments.text: BOARD MEMBER CARLSON AND THEN CLENDENIN.

segments.speaker: BILL CARLSON
segments.text: MY FRUSTRATION, AND FOR ANYBODY WATCHING FOR THE FIRST TIME, I MET WITH WILLIE ROBINSON IN FRONT OF THE HOUSE IN 2012, I THINK IT WAS, WHEN HE HAD JUST GOTTEN AN ORDER FROM MAYOR BUCKHORN, TEAR IT DOWN AND CHARGE 60,000 IN FEES AND CHARGE HIM FOR TEARING IT DOWN. AND WE SAVED IT. LINDA SAUL-SENA CAME IN. CITY COUNCIL OVERRULED THE MAYOR'S ORDER AT THE TIME. THEN WE TRIED TO SAVE IT AND THE MAYOR AT THE TIME SQUASHED OUR PROJECT TO SAVE IT. THEN IT ROLLED INTO THE FOUNDATION, SOMEWHERE AROUND 2013. BUT FROM THE POINT OF VIEW OF THE PUBLIC, NOTHING HAS BEEN DONE SINCE 2013. I KNOW STEEL BEAMS AND THINGS DONE INSIDE. THE REALITY IS THE THING IS FALLING APART. THE SIDES ARE FALLING OFF AND THAT'S WHAT THE PUBLIC SEES. OFFERED TO BUY IT FROM THE JACKSON HOUSE FOUNDATION. WE OFFERED TO CONDEMN IT AND THEN GIVE IT BACK TO THE FOUNDATION. THE FOUNDATION IS LIKE WE WANT TO RUN IT, WE WANT TO RUN IT. THE THING IS FALLING APART AND THE PUBLIC DOESN'T SEE ANYTHING. WE ALLOCATED THE MONEY AROUND 2019 AND THERE WERE CONCERNS ABOUT ACCESS. ACCARDIS GAVE TEMPORARY ACCESS. CONFIRM WITH THE FOUNDATION, YOU HAVE ACCESS ON BOTH SIDES AND IN THE ALLEY NOW? TEN FEET EASEMENT ON THE EAST AND WEST SIDE OF THE HOUSE.

segments.speaker: BILL CARLSON
segments.text: SORRY TO BRING YOU BACK UP. CHAIR. WE ACTUALLY HAVE THE TEN FEET EASEMENT ON THE EAST AND WEST SIDE OF THE HOUSE. THANKS TO THE CITY OF TAMPA, WE WERE NOT ABLE TO GET IT AFTER WORKING OVER THREE YEARS PLUS, BUT THE CITY WAS ABLE TO GET IT. THAT'S WHY WE'RE GRATEFUL TO EVERYONE. ONCE THE CITY GOT IT, THEY GOT IT AND THEN TOLD US DO WHAT YOU NEED TO DO. WE HAD TO DO EVERYTHING THEY TOLD US TO DO AND WE HAVE THE DEED. YES, WE OWN THAT. IN ADDITION, WHILE WE DID NOT WANT TO CLOSE THE ALLEY, WE CLOSED THE ALLEY IN GOOD FAITH WORKING WITH THE ACCARDIS THAT WORKED THROUGH THE CITY AND WE'VE GAINED ADDITIONAL PROPERTY AT THE END -- AT THE BACK OF THE HOUSE WHICH GIVE US HALF OF THE ALLEY AS WELL.

segments.speaker: BILL CARLSON
segments.text: SEVEN OR -- I WAS TOLD BY THE CITY THAT THE JACKSON HOUSE, ACCARDIS AND THE CITY, WOULD GO DOWN AND DO THE SURVEY AGAIN. WE CAN SEE THE MARKERS WHERE SOMEONE HAS BEEN THERE. SOMEONE TOLD -- I SAID DON'T CALL THE CITY NO MORE. EASY FOR PEOPLE TO SAY ONE THING TO ME OR US TOGETHER AND THEN SAY ANOTHER THING TO HER AND THEN WE HAVE TO UNDO IT. WE WERE TOLD WE WOULD GO DOWN TOGETHER, DO THE SURVEY, THEN THEY SAY, OH, NO, WE DIDN'T SAY DO THAT. OH, YES, YOU DID. IF WE HAVE TO, WE'LL PAY FOR THE SURVEY.

segments.speaker: BILL CARLSON
segments.text: IN 2019 AFTER WE ALLOCATED THIS MILLION DOLLARS, JEFF VINIK VIA HIS THEN CHIEF OF STAFF CHRISTINA BARKER ANNOUNCED THAT THE VINIK FOUNDATION WAS GIVING A MILLION DOLLARS. I UNDERSTOOD THAT MS. BARKER THEN WAS ON YOUR BOARD ALSO. NEVER BEEN ON THE BOARD.

segments.speaker: BILL CARLSON
segments.text: THANK YOU FOR CLARIFYING THAT. WHAT IS THE STATUS OF THAT MONEY? IS THAT NOT COMING NOW? THAT, BUT THE TAMPA BAY HISTORY CENTER THAT MR. VINIK WANTED TO GIVE THE MONEY TO MAKE SURE IT WAS APPROPRIATELY MANAGE AND HE ASKED FOR OUR PERMISSION TO DO THAT AND WE AGREED. WHEN CJ ROBERTS LEFT, CJ ROBERTS, WHATEVER HE DID, HE DID. IT'S OUT THERE. THEY SENT ALL OF THE MONEY AND THE RECORDS BACK TO THE VINIK FOUNDATION. AS FAR AS WE'RE CONCERNED, THE VINIK FOUNDATION STILL HAVE THE FUNDS. THE VINIKS HAVE NOT SAID THEY ARE NOT GOING TO GIVE US THE FUNDS AT ALL. I TALKED TO CHRISTINA BARKER ON A NUMBER OF OCCASIONS. SHE SAID THEY WAS WAITING AS WELL TO SEE PROGRESS. EVEN UNDER THE TAMPA BAY HISTORY CENTER, THEY WAS NOT SEEING IT.

segments.speaker: BILL CARLSON
segments.text: POLICY DIRECTOR UNDER THE MAYOR TRYING TO TEAR IT DOWN. COMMUNITY HAS CONCERNS ABOUT THAT. WHY DID IT TAKE FROM 2019 UNTIL RECENTLY -- UNTIL THREE YEARS AGO FOR ANYBODY TO TELL THE FOUNDATION THAT WE HAD ALLOCATED THE MILLION DOLLARS?

segments.speaker: BILL CARLSON
segments.text: I DON'T KNOW WHY SOMEBODY ON STAFF OR AT THE CITY WOULDN'T HAVE TOLD. WHILE SHE'S GETTING UP TO ANSWER THAT, I'M IN FAVOR OF EXPEDITING SOME PART OF THE MONEY. I'M IN FAVOR OF ASKING FOR ADDITIONAL MONEY. BUT WHAT I WANT TO SEE IS MOVEMENT ON RENOVATING IT. THE PUBLIC WANTS TO SEE MOVEMENT. PIECES ARE FALLING DOWN AND DON'T SEE ANY ACTION HAPPENING. IF YOU CAN COME BACK IN LET'S SAY TWO MONTHS WITH A LOT OF PROGRESS BEING SHOWN -- WE CAN COME BACK TO YOU IN HOPEFULLY AS SOON AS WE HAVE THE COMPANY THAT WAS THERE YESTERDAY WITH THE THREE COMPANIES THEY HAVE CALLED TO DO WHAT THEY NEED TO DO. WE HAVE A MEETING TODAY WITH THE STATE TO GET PERMISSION FOR IT.

segments.speaker: BILL CARLSON
segments.text: WE WOULD APPROVE THIS MONEY TODAY HOPEFULLY WITH A CLAUSE THAT IT NEEDS TO BE SUBSTANTIALLY COMPLETED WITHIN A YEAR. BUT THE OTHER THING, IF YOU NEED ADDITIONAL MONEY, I'M HAPPY TO MAKE A MOTION FOR THAT AT SOME POINT, BUT I NEED TO SEE MAJOR CHANGES GOING ON AT THE FACILITY. MY FRUSTRATION FOR THE PUBLIC IS NOT WITH YOU INDIVIDUALLY. IT'S THE FACT THAT THIS THING IS FALLING APART AND THERE ARE POLITICAL FORCES IN THE COMMUNITY WHO WANT IT TO FALL APART AND ARE GOING TO CLAP AND CELEBRATE WHEN IT FALLS APART. I THINK IT'S TOO IMPORTANT OF A BUILDING IN AFRICAN AMERICAN HISTORY AND TAMPA'S HISTORY, AND I PERSONALLY PROMISED WILLIE ROBINSON THAT I WOULD HELP SAVE IT. I'M ANGRY BECAUSE THE THING IS FALLING APART. I PROMISED WILLIE THAT I WOULD DO THE SAME THING. WE'RE DOING EVERYTHING WE CAN. I WOULD ASK BECAUSE WE JUST FOUND OUT ABOUT THE MONEY, WHEN WE WERE STANDING HERE, THAT YOU HAD GIVEN US A MILLION DOLLARS AND WE DID NOT KNOW ANYTHING ABOUT IT, BUT WE GOT THE MILLION DOLLARS FROM THE STATE PROBABLY ABOUT THREE YEARS BEFORE THEN, AND THEY HAVE WORKED WITH US WITH THE GRANT. I WOULD ASK THAT YOU GUYS PASS THIS TODAY. IF YOU HAVE ANY QUESTIONS AND YOU WANT US TO COME BACK WITH WHATEVER, WE'RE MORE THAN WELCOME -- I MEAN, WE'RE GOING TO DO WHAT YOU ASK US TO DO. WE'VE HAD TO WAIT. DO WE NEED MORE MONEY? WE'VE ALREADY TOLD YOU THAT. AS SOON AS SIGN THE CONTRACT WITH THE CONTRACTOR, CONSTRUCTION FIRM, TO COME BACK, HAVE THEM DO A BUDGET AND BRING IT BACK. WE'LL GO THROUGH YOUR NEW PROCESS. THAT'S WHAT THEY TOLD US WE NEEDED TO DO, THAT WE HAD TO START OVER AGAIN, GO THROUGH THE NEW PROCESS ALL OVER IN ORDER TO GET THE ADDITIONAL MONEY AND WE'RE GOING TO JUMP THROUGH THOSE AND HOPEFULLY WE'LL BE DOING THAT WITHIN A MONTH.
